headline: State Government Issues Circular Requiring All Citizens to Physically Sigh Loudly Whenever They Pass a Construction Site
body:
The state administration has officially mandated that all citizens must perform a 'audible expression of moral disapproval'—specifically a long, weary sigh—whenever they pass a public infrastructure project to signal their zero-tolerance stance toward corruption. The initiative, titled 'The Breath of Integrity,' aims to ensure that no road, bridge, or sidewalk is constructed without a synchronized soundtrack of collective public skepticism.

'We believe that true transparency starts with the lungs,' explained a senior official from the Department of Civic Vigilance. 'If every taxpaying citizen exhales in disappointment while walking past an under-construction flyover, the sheer volume of air pressure will naturally inhibit any potential for bribery by making the contractors feel slightly awkward.'

The circular further notes that high-decibel sighs will be recorded by local traffic cameras, with the data being uploaded to a central 'Integrity Dashboard.' Citizens who fail to demonstrate adequate levels of respiratory disapproval may be sent a soft-copy notification asking them to consider if they are doing enough to build a cleaner future. 

Construction companies have welcomed the move, noting that the constant background sighing has significantly improved the mood of their workers, who now feel they are working in a perpetual, dramatic movie scene.
caption: New govt circular asks citizens to sigh at construction sites to combat corruption. Who knew transparency was just a deep breath away? 💨🏗️ #TamilNadu #Governance #CivicDuty #Transparency (satire)
